x: Whitlock and Hopkins made clear their claims beyond any shadow of doubt, and T. Lloyd Johnson, although failing on this occasion, has sterling performances to his credit in the past.
In the last few yards, however, Lloyd Johnson managed to pass Fred Rickards and so took his club into second position, and relegated us to third place, one point separating us.

However, Fred has learned some philosophy in the course of many years' walking, and met misfortune with a smile. A week later he walked Lloyd Johnson to a yard in 25 miles, both men being well inside previous record!

Anyway, this year's double-first and third is very creditable to all concerned, and the Club can regard these performances with great pride. In Lewis's 25 Miles round Birmingham Walk, Fred Rickards was beaten by a yard by T.
Surprise of the race was the excellent performance of Lloyd Johnson who finished 2nd to Rex Whitlock and gave the Olympic Selectors something to think about.

At the start the two Sheffield lads, Allen and Proctor, made a quick getaway and joined by Lloyd Johnson, set up a good pace. Lloyd however, did not last with them for long and soon began to drop back.

Although we were beaten into second place, our boys put up a grand show and walked splendidly throughout—but stay, before we sing our own praises, let us first congratulate a very gallant team, Woodford Green, in their triumph which they achieved after fighting hard for so many years; the splendid w…
The start was a fairly fast one with Proctor, Lloyd Johnson, Martineau and Clayton well up in the lead. Proctor soon went away taking advantage of the home ground and knowing the course well.
Second was the " retired, but can't " walker, Lloyd Johnson, a very fine performance for a man of 51 years. Training for next year's Olympic Games is my bet.

All the great British long distance walkers and many of those from abroad have competed in this race, including Olympic medallists Tommy Green, Harold Whitlock, Lloyd Johnson, Don Thompson, Norman Read and Abdon Pamich.
Tommy was placed three times in this event. In 1930 at Derby he finished 3rd behind A.E.Plumb (North London H) and T.

We are very glad to see Tommy Green out again, and although he is not yet his old self, he has already been responsible for some very fine performances. Best of these, perhaps, was to beat T. Lloyd Johnson, the National 20 miles and 50 kilometres champion, in a 25 miles race at Manchester.
